speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with yellowish discoloration of your skin; have you noticed this jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of birth?

REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin, Direct_Bilirubin, Hemoglobin, Reticulocyte_Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Total_Bilirubin: 7 mg/dL, Direct_Bilirubin: 0.6 mg/dL, Hemoglobin: 17.6 g/dL, Reticulocyte_Count: 0.3%

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is highly unusual, as acute appendicitis does not present with jaundice in a newborn; can you confirm your actual age in hours or days? Additionally, has your baby been breastfeeding well, or is there any history of bruising, bleeding, or blood in the stool?

REQUEST TEST: G6PD_Level, Thyroid_Stimulation_Hormone (TSH).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: G6PD_Level: Normal, Thyroid_Stimulation_Hormone (TSH): Normal READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological Jaundice (due to normal TSH and G6PD, and onset pattern, though the mention of appendicitis is a severe misdiagnosis). I recommend a follow-up bilirubin check in 24 hours to ensure levels remain within safe limits and monitor for any progression.
